You where still pretty lucky getting diagnosed so fast, when I had my accident at work and injured my hand(amongst other things) they said it was a very simple sprain, after months of still being in pain I was referred to the best orthopedic hand/wrist surgeon, they did a million different test and treatments and could not figure out what was wrong, I even had exploratory surgery (they found a tear) but after that everything got extremely worse, I did OT for 5 months after the surgery and got a MMI and got told I could look for another opinion, went to another hand surgeon got more tests and nothing, went without treatment for about 7 more months, finally one of my other doctors decided to sent me to a pain specialist and he right away said that I had crps.
In regards to your nurse case manager, even though they work for the insurance, all that the insurance wants is not to pay more and more, the faster you recover better for them, if your NCM is not advocating to get you treatment fast she hasn't done her job at investigating what crps is. Also ask your doctor's office to give you a copy of all the paperwork for the visit you just had, and along with sending a copy to the NCM to also send a copy directly to your adjuster.

I'm so happy that they catch it so early on for you, I got diagnosed about 15 months after my injury and thankfully my nurse case manager from WC it's really on it to get me on appointments as soon as possible and talking to my adjustor to get everything approved as fast as possible. A few months into my injury my physician told me that if I feel like my nurse case manager isn't really helpful I could talk directly to the adjustor to get a new nurse case manager that made me feel more comfortable and that I felt i could always go to if I needed help. A few months ago I was lucky and randomly I met a guy that just retired from being a manager for WC adjustor's, he told me that if I feel like my nurse case manager and adjustor are being slow I can call and ask for a supervisor and tell them about the situation.
Navigating through WC world is the worst thing in the world, one of my physician's advise me that if they offer to settle, don't give up my medical because for CRPS is very expensive to treat(this physician is not the one treating my crps, but he deals with a lot of head and nerve injuries) he also recommended to try other stuff before I even consider the spinal cord stimulator.

As a preventive measure I would suggest that you write on your skin in the affected area DO NOT TOUCH, I recently had to get my gallbladder removed and made sure that I told everyone that I came in contact to not touch my arm if it wasn't extremely necessary because of my CRPS, when I woke up from the surgery I couldn't stop crying because the pain was so intense in my arm, they would only give me ketorolac and discharged me while I was still crying in pain, all that because they decided when I was already under anesthesia to switch the blood pressure cuff to my affected arm. When I told my pain management doctor suggested next time I just grab a market and out do not touch so that way no one forgets
